title: Here Comes the Fire Truck
why: A familiar rescue song to lead into new adventures.
play: Pretend a cushion is a fire. Ask: what could we use to reach it?

title: Digging in the Dirt
why: Keep the digger excitement; act out how different machines work.
play: Use your arms as a digger, then a bulldozer. Say what each machine does.

title: Driving in My Car
why: Switch between travelling on land, water and in the air.
play: Line up a car, boat and plane. Let Lucas choose which one you sing about.

title: Walking in the Jungle
why: An adventure with repeated action words and animal discoveries.
play: Explore the room together. Pause and let Lucas choose the next movement.

title: The Farmer in the Dell
why: Choose Caitie’s farm-chores version: more to describe than animal noises.
play: Pretend to plant seeds, water them and gather eggs. What might a tractor help with?

title: A Sailor Went to Sea
why: A repeating tune for discovering sea creatures together.
play: Make a pretend boat, then name the animals you might see below it.

title: Open Shut Them
why: Make opposite ideas visible with your hands, voice and whole body.
play: Make a big garage and a small garage with your arms for toy trucks.

title: How’s the Weather?
why: A short question-and-answer song you can use at the window each day.
play: Look outside after singing. Describe today’s sky and choose what to wear.

title: How Are You Feeling?
why: Link a feeling word with an expressive face or an action.
play: Make a face together. Offer your own feeling first, then invite his.

title: Put On Your Shoes
why: Turn clothing words into a real getting-ready routine.
play: Let a teddy get dressed too. Swap in the clothes you actually need today.

title: The Ants Go Marching
why: A steady marching beat, counting and repeated rhyming endings.
play: March with toy animals. Start with a few verses; let him fill a familiar ending.

title: Down by the Bay
why: A playful refrain with room to invent your own surprising rhymes. The official upload is audio with a still picture.
play: Take turns inventing a silly animal rhyme. It need not make sense; enjoy how the words sound.

title: The Goldfish (Let’s Go Swimming)
why: Follow a longer comic sequence, act out the fish’s mistakes and return to the repeated chorus.
play: Pause after a silly activity and ask what a fish would really do. Invent a new verse together.

title: Rocketship Run
why: A pretend rocket journey with movement cues, a returning chorus and a fuller band arrangement. A playful bridge from vehicles to space.
play: Build a pretend rocket and act out a countdown. Retell the stops in order. Treat the journey as imagination, rather than a lesson in space travel.

title: Can You Canoe?
why: A melodic folk duet with a repeated invitation and a river-adventure setting; a change from nursery-song arrangements.
play: Make a cushion canoe and plan a trip: what would you pack, and where would you stop? Notice the string instruments.

title: The Prepositions Song
why: Use position words to describe where things are, then put them into your own instructions.
play: Hide a toy truck and give clues using position words. Swap who gives and follows the clues.

title: The Counting by Twos Song
why: A steady counting pattern to connect to real pairs, rather than only memorising a number sequence.
play: Line up pairs of socks or toy wheels. Count each object, then count by pairs and compare the totals.

title: The Water Cycle Song
why: A repeating song for naming water-cycle processes; connect each new term to something you can observe.
play: Notice a drying puddle and droplets on the outside of a cold glass. Draw arrows to tell a drop’s journey; a song is an introduction, not a complete explanation.

title: The Planets of Our Solar System Song (Update)
artist: Hopscotch Songs feat. The Hoover Jam
why: A longer song with separate planet sections, new descriptive words and a returning chorus.
play: Choose one planet per listen. Draw it, say one thing you noticed and ask one question to investigate. Pictures and spacing in the song are not to scale.

title: Seven Continents Song (Oceania Version)
why: Use a memorable tune to explore a seven-continent naming convention and locate broad regions on a globe.
play: Find Australia and then a place connected to someone you know. This version says Oceania for the wider region; maps may instead label the continent Australia.

title: Meet the Elements
why: An upbeat band song introduces the idea that materials are made of elements; enjoy the chorus before trying to explain every term.
play: Pick one material mentioned and look for it at home. Use models to discuss combining atoms; do not expect the whole song to be understood on the first listen.

title: Photosynthesis
why: A catchy rock song opens a conversation about how plants use light to make sugars, with technical vocabulary to revisit slowly.
play: Look at a plant together and name what it needs. Draw sunlight, water and air going in, and explain that light provides energy to make sugars.

title: Do-Re-Mi (Official Lyric Video)
artist: The Sound of Music / Rodgers & Hammerstein
why: A musical-theatre song with rising note names, wordplay and longer phrases; start with the repeating note-name section.
play: Make your hand move higher as the notes rise. Echo just a short phrase, then make up your own three-note tune. The English wordplay is a memory aid for the syllables.
